name: ahd_search_qinfifo
prose: Precondition: ahd is an initialised aic79xx softc with the sequencer paused. Postcondition: it saves the chip modes and switches to CCHAN mode, stops any pending SCB DMA (busy-waiting until CCARREN/CCSCBEN clear), and rebuilds the qinfifo from the sequencer's position: ahd->qinfifonext is set to the sequencer offset and every qinfifo entry is looked up with ahd_lookup_scb; a NULL result panics ('Loop 1'). Each SCB matching (target, channel, lun, tag, role) is counted in the return value and, for SEARCH_COMPLETE (printing 'Inactive SCB in qinfifo' if it was not SCB_ACTIVE), completed with ahd_done_with_status and not requeued, for SEARCH_REMOVE dropped, and for SEARCH_COUNT and SEARCH_PRINT requeued; non-matching SCBs are requeued in order. It then writes the new queue offset with ahd_set_hnscb_qoff. In SCSI mode it walks the waiting-for-selection TID list: it panics if the list has more than AHD_NUM_TARGETS entries, if an SCB index is not below scb_data.numscbs (after dumping the card state) or if an entry does not resolve to an SCB; for each list whose target matches it calls ahd_search_scb_list (adding its count), handles a pending MK_MESSAGE SCB that matches (counted; for SEARCH_COMPLETE/REMOVE it is completed for COMPLETE, the per-target tail is reset, PENDING_MK_MESSAGE cleared and CMDS_PENDING decremented; for COUNT/PRINT it is left), re-queues a still-pending MK_MESSAGE SCB when the last SCB of a matching target list is removed, and re-stitches the TID list when its head changed. It finally restores SCBPTR and the saved modes and returns the number of matches found in the qinfifo, the waiting lists and the MK_MESSAGE SCB.
note: reviewer (round 15: an inactive SCB does not panic, it is only printed) right, aic79xx_core.c:8170-8171; the panics are for NULL lookups, an over-long TID list and an out-of-range waiting SCB index (8160, 8219, 8226, 8232). The old prose also said every entry resolves to an 'active' SCB, which the code does not require. Function at 8100-8327; ahd_search_scb_list was not read.

name: ahc_build_transfer_msg
prose: Precondition: ahc and devinfo are valid, ahc_fetch_transinfo gives the initiator tinfo for devinfo, and ahc->msgout_buf has room at ahc->msgout_index for the message (at most 8 bytes). Postcondition: it takes the goal period, offset and ppr_options from tinfo->goal (ppr_options forced to 0 for ROLE_TARGET) and limits them with ahc_devlimited_syncrate. dowide is true when the current width differs from the goal width, dosync when the current offset or period differs from the goal values, and doppr when the limited ppr_options are non-zero. If none is true it sets dowide when the goal width is not 8-bit and dosync when the goal offset is non-zero; if still none is true it sets dowide on an AHC_WIDE controller (forcing async with a WDTR) or dosync otherwise (an SDTR with zero offset). For ROLE_TARGET doppr is then cleared. It appends exactly one message: a PPR if doppr is true, else an SDTR if dosync is true and dowide is false, else a WDTR with the goal width; when both a width and a sync change are needed only the WDTR is built. The message advances msgout_index and increases msgout_len by 8 (PPR), 5 (SDTR) or 4 (WDTR). Nothing is returned and no lock is taken.
note: reviewer (round 15: an SDTR can be built when no sync change was needed, because dosync is set from a non-zero goal offset) right; the earlier 'iff a sync change is needed' wording was too strict. aic7xxx_core.c:2937-3028; lengths from msgout_len += lines 3042, 3060, 3082.

name: tscam
prose: Precondition: host is a Scsi_Host whose hostdata is an atp_unit with a valid host_id[0]; wide_chip tells whether 16 IDs are used and scam_on holds the SCAM enable bits; the I/O registers are accessible. Postcondition: returns nothing. It writes registers 0x01, 0x02 and 0x11 on channel 0 and returns if (scam_on & 0x40) == 0. Otherwise it builds a local assign-id bitmap (the host's ID bit, and bits 8-15 for a narrow chip), probes the remaining IDs in turn with register writes, waiting on status bit 0x80 of register 0x1f with unbounded loops, and adds IDs that answer to the bitmap; it then drives the bus signals for the SCAM selection and enters a loop that has no exit except one return: if BSY is found clear at the top of an iteration it clears registers 0x1c, 0x1b and 0x15, writes 0x09 to 0x18, waits for status bit 0x80, reads register 0x17 and returns. Otherwise each iteration runs the isolation and ID-string reads (stored in the local array mbuf), picks an unassigned ID from the bitmap, builds the two quintet bytes in the local array quintet and sends them with fun_scam. mbuf and quintet are local arrays, not buffers supplied by the caller, and the function may wait indefinitely on hardware status bits.
note: the name in the listed item was 'unnamed scam device assignment routine'; the function is tscam (atp870u.c:1014-1234), read in full. The old prose treated mbuf and quintet as caller buffers and described a 'completes the scan' return that does not exist.

name: atp870u_intr_handle
prose: Precondition: dev_id is the Scsi_Host whose hostdata is an initialised atp_unit and whose I/O registers are accessible. Postcondition: it reads status register 0x1f of channel 0 and then channel 1 (clearing dev->in_int[c] for each channel it passes over) and stops at the first channel whose value has bit 0x80 set; if neither channel has it, it returns IRQ_NONE. Otherwise it sets dev->in_int[c] to 1 and processes the interrupt for that channel by status (updating request and transfer state, programming adapter registers, taking host_lock around parts of the work, and clearing in_int[c] on paths that finish a status), and returns IRQ_HANDLED on every other return path.
note: listed name atp870u_intr_handler does not exist; the function is atp870u_intr_handle (atp870u.c:119-619). The old prose said it never returns IRQ_NONE, but line 140 does. Partly read: lines 119-200 in detail, and every return, spin_lock and IRQ_ value in the rest was located by grep; the middle of the body was not read line by line.

name: bfad_iocmd_handler
prose: Precondition: bfad is the bfad_s instance, cmd is an IOCMD_* code, iocmd points to the command buffer and payload_len is its length. Postcondition: it starts with rc = -EINVAL and dispatches on cmd with a switch of one case per supported IOCMD_* code, each calling the matching bfad_iocmd_* handler and storing its return value in rc (some pass payload_len or cmd as well); an unrecognised cmd leaves rc at -EINVAL. It returns rc, that is, whatever the selected handler returned (the handlers' own return values are not enumerated here), or -EINVAL for an unknown command.
note: listed name bfad_iocmd does not exist; the function is bfad_iocmd_handler (bfad_bsg.c:2774-3146). Only the head, the tail and the case count were read; the handlers were not read, so their return values are not described.

name: bfad_chk_iocmd_sz
note: bfad_chk_iocmd_sz is a preprocessor macro in bfad_bsg.h:825-827 (an expression yielding BFA_STATUS_FAILED when payload_len != hdrsz + bufsz, else BFA_STATUS_OK), not a function.

name: bfad_im_itnim_work_handler
prose: Precondition: work is the itnim_work member of a bfad_itnim_s that was queued on a workqueue. Postcondition: returns nothing; it takes bfad->bfad_lock with interrupts saved, drops and retakes it around bfad_im_fc_rport_add and around fc_remote_port_delete, and returns with it released. For ITNIM_STATE_ONLINE with itnim->fc_rport NULL it calls bfad_im_fc_rport_add, which stores the result of fc_remote_port_add in itnim->fc_rport (possibly NULL) and, only when that returned an rport, sets maxframe size, supported classes, the dd_data back-pointer and, when valid, scsi_tgt_id and the channel (nothing is set when fc_remote_port_add fails); it then, whether or not an rport exists, adds itnim to im_port->itnim_mapped_list and logs 'ITNIM ONLINE'; with fc_rport already set it only prints a warning. For ITNIM_STATE_OFFLINE_PENDING it sets the state to ITNIM_STATE_OFFLINE and, if itnim->fc_rport is set, clears the dd_data back-pointer and itnim->fc_rport, sets dev_loss_tmo and calls fc_remote_port_delete unless BFAD_PORT_DELETE is set in the port flags, removes itnim from its list and logs 'ITNIM OFFLINE'. For ITNIM_STATE_FREE it does the same back-pointer clearing, conditional fc_remote_port_delete and list removal when fc_rport is set, and in every case kfrees the itnim while still holding bfad_lock. Any other state only calls WARN_ON(1).
note: reviewer (round 15: scsi_tgt_id/channel are not set when fc_remote_port_add fails) right, bfad_im.c:1075-1076; round 2 (ONLINE path lists and logs even on failure) is reflected. Function at bfad_im.c:1104-1197, helper 1058-1097.

name: bfad_im_port_clean_helper
note: no function by this name in bfad_im.c; the nearby function is bfad_im_port_clean (651-668), but the packet gives no prose, so which function was meant cannot be told.

name: bnx2fc_enable
prose: Precondition: netdev is a network device. Postcondition: it takes rtnl_lock and then bnx2fc_dev_lock and releases both before returning. It looks up the interface for netdev; if none exists it logs and returns -ENODEV. Otherwise it returns __bnx2fc_enable(ctlr): if the interface is not yet enabled and ctlr->lp is NULL, that returns -ENODEV; if the interface is not enabled and lp exists, then when bnx2fc_link_ok(lport) returns 0 (the physical device is up and has carrier) it calls fcoe_ctlr_link_up and sets interface->enabled to true, and when it returns -1 neither happens and enabled stays false. Independently of the enabled state (but only when the interface got past the -ENODEV check), if the hba, hba->cnic, the lport, lport->host and cnic->get_fc_npiv_tbl exist it allocates an NPIV table, reads it and, if that succeeds, creates the static NPIV vports; an allocation or table-read failure there is ignored. Both of those cases return 0.
note: reviewer (round 15: NPIV vports are created even when already enabled or when link_ok fails) right, bnx2fc_fcoe.c:2184-2210; round 2 (link_ok failure leaves it disabled, return 0) also right. bnx2fc_link_ok returns 0 when the link is up (761-776), so 'link_ok succeeds' in the old text matched. Function at 2220-2241 with __bnx2fc_enable at 2167-2215.

name: bnx2fc_indicate_netevent
prose: Precondition: context is a bnx2fc_hba, event is a NETDEV_* value and vlan_id the associated VLAN id. Postcondition: returns nothing. It returns at once if vlan_id != 0 and event != NETDEV_UNREGISTER. For NETDEV_UNREGISTER with vlan_id == 0, and for any event other than UP, DOWN, GOING_DOWN, CHANGE and UNREGISTER, it returns at once; for NETDEV_UNREGISTER with a non-zero vlan_id it destroys, under bnx2fc_dev_lock, every interface on if_list whose hba is context and whose vlan_id equals vlan_id & VLAN_VID_MASK, and returns. For UP it only logs if ADAPTER_STATE_UP is clear; DOWN clears ADAPTER_STATE_GOING_DOWN and ADAPTER_STATE_UP and sets link_possible to 0; GOING_DOWN sets ADAPTER_STATE_GOING_DOWN and clears link_possible; CHANGE changes nothing. Then, under bnx2fc_dev_lock, for each interface of this hba it refreshes the link speed and: if link_possible is set and bnx2fc_link_ok(lport) returns 0 (link up), then for a ctlr in state FCOE_CTLR_DISABLED it only logs, and for FCOE_CTLR_ENABLED or FCOE_CTLR_UNUSED it resets the MFS and calls fcoe_ctlr_link_up if interface->enabled is set; otherwise (link not possible or link not up), if fcoe_ctlr_link_down(ctlr) returns non-zero, a DISABLED ctlr only logs and an ENABLED or UNUSED one has its vports' and lport's port type set to FC_PORTTYPE_UNKNOWN, LinkFailureCount incremented, the pending queue cleaned and wait_for_upload set. After releasing the lock, if wait_for_upload is set it clears ADAPTER_STATE_READY, reinitialises hba->shutdown_wait, sets hba->wait_for_link_down to 1, waits interruptibly until hba->num_ofld_sess is 0 (it may return early on a signal), sets wait_for_link_down back to 0 and flushes pending signals.
note: reviewer (round 15: omits the log-only branch when the controller is disabled) is a minor omission, now stated; the old prose's 'the link is not ok' was also the wrong way round, since bnx2fc_link_ok returns 0 for link-up (bnx2fc_fcoe.c:761-776). Function at 858-980.

name: csio_config_device_caps
prose: Precondition: hw is an initialised HW module with a mailbox mempool. Postcondition: it allocates one mailbox buffer from hw->mb_mempool; if that fails it increments the nomem counter and returns -ENOMEM (nothing to free). Otherwise the buffer is freed on every later return. It issues a read FW_CAPS_CONFIG_CMD: if issuing fails or the firmware return value is not FW_SUCCESS it returns -EINVAL; it then validates the capabilities with csio_hw_validate_caps and returns its non-zero result if validation fails; if hw->fw_state == CSIO_DEV_STATE_INIT it returns 0 without writing. Otherwise it issues the write FW_CAPS_CONFIG_CMD, and if issuing it fails or the firmware return value is not FW_SUCCESS it also returns -EINVAL; it returns 0 only when the write succeeds. No lock is held at return.
note: reviewer (round 15: write-command issue or retval failures return -EINVAL, not 0) right: rv starts at -EINVAL and is only set to 0 at line 1495. Function at csio_hw.c:1443-1499.

name: csio_do_hello
prose: Precondition: hw is an initialised HW module with a valid hw->pfn and a mailbox mempool, state points to a caller-provided csio_dev_state, and the caller holds hw->lock with interrupts disabled (the function drops and retakes it with spin_unlock_irq/spin_lock_irq while waiting). Postcondition: it allocates a mailbox buffer (-ENOMEM and a nomem count if that fails), issues HELLO, and frees the buffer on every path after allocation. If csio_mb_issue fails it returns that function's error; if the firmware return value is not FW_SUCCESS it returns -EINVAL. If hw->pfn equals the master PF from the response it sets CSIO_HWF_MASTER. Otherwise, if *state is CSIO_DEV_STATE_UNINIT, it polls PCIE_FW every 50 ms (with hw->lock dropped around each sleep): when the firmware shows error or initialised it sets *state to CSIO_DEV_STATE_ERR (and rv to -ETIMEDOUT) or CSIO_DEV_STATE_INIT, may adopt the master PF from the register, and stops; if neither shows within FW_CMD_HELLO_TIMEOUT it re-issues HELLO while retries remain and otherwise returns -ETIMEDOUT; it then clears CSIO_HWF_MASTER. It logs the final state and returns 0 unless one of the errors above occurred.
note: reviewer (round 15: the caller must hold hw->lock, since the function unlocks and relocks it) right, csio_hw.c:980-982. Round 0 (csio_mb_issue's error is returned) is reflected. Function at 916-1055.

name: cxgb4_dcb_change_notify
prose: Precondition: data points to a dcb_app_type; self and val are unused. Postcondition: returns NOTIFY_DONE, before any logging or lookup, when the event's dcbx has neither IEEE nor CEE support, when an IEEE selector is neither STREAM nor ANY, when a CEE selector is not PORTNUM, when a CEE priority is zero, or when the protocol is not 3260. For the others it computes the priority (the IEEE app priority, or for CEE ffs(app.priority) - 1), logs a debug message, and calls dev_get_by_index; if there is no net device it returns NOTIFY_DONE (after the debug log). Otherwise it looks up the cxgbi device for that net device, releases the net-device reference with dev_put, and returns NOTIFY_DONE if no cxgbi device exists; else for each port_csk entry i < pmap->used that is non-NULL and whose dcb_priority differs from the priority it calls iscsi_conn_failure(ISCSI_ERR_CONN_FAILED) and logs, and returns NOTIFY_OK.
note: reviewer (round 15: the no-netdev path logs a debug message before returning) right, cxgb4i.c:2412-2417. Function at 2381-2441.

name: disconnect
prose: Precondition: acb->active_dcb is NULL or the active device block whose active_srb points at the request block for the disconnecting command. Postcondition: if acb->active_dcb is NULL it only delays 500 us, sets acb->last_reset to jiffies + HZ/2 + HZ * eeprom.delay_time, clears the FIFO and writes DO_HWRESELECT. Otherwise it takes srb from dcb->active_srb, clears acb->active_dcb, sets srb->scsi_phase to PH_BUS_FREE, clears the FIFO, writes DO_HWRESELECT and then: if SRB_UNEXPECT_RESEL is set in srb->state it zeroes the state and calls waiting_process_next; else if SRB_ABORT_SENT is set it clears ABORT_DEV_ in dcb->flag, sets last_reset to jiffies + HZ/2 + 1, calls doing_srb_done with DID_ABORT and waiting_process_next; otherwise, if the state has SRB_START_ or SRB_MSGOUT set, or has neither SRB_DISCONNECT nor SRB_COMPLETED: if the state is not exactly SRB_START_ or SRB_MSGOUT it sets the state to SRB_READY and target_status to SCSI_STAT_SEL_TIMEOUT and completes the command as below; otherwise it post-increments srb->retry_count and, if the value before the increment was above DC395x_MAX_RETRIES or acb->scan_devices is set, sets target_status to SCSI_STAT_SEL_TIMEOUT and completes the command as below, else it frees the tag, moves srb to dcb->srb_waiting_list and arms the waiting timer for HZ/20. If instead SRB_DISCONNECT is set it reads the SCSI signal register and, unless bit 0x40 is set (nothing more is done then), calls waiting_process_next. If SRB_COMPLETED is set it completes the command. Completing the command means: free the tag, clear dcb->active_srb, set srb->state to SRB_FREE and call srb_done.
note: reviewer (round 15: the retry check uses the pre-increment value) right, dc395x.c:2490. Function at 2445-2520.

name: alua_rtpg
prose: Precondition: sdev is a live scsi_device and pg is an alua_port_group the caller holds a reference to; the caller holds neither pg->lock nor port_group_lock. Postcondition: it returns one of SCSI_DH_OK, SCSI_DH_RETRY, SCSI_DH_IO, SCSI_DH_DEV_TEMP_BUSY, SCSI_DH_RES_TEMP_UNAVAIL or SCSI_DH_DEV_OFFLINED, with its temporary buffer freed on every path and every reference taken by alua_find_get_pg released. If pg->expiry is 0 on entry it is first set to round_jiffies_up(jiffies + (pg->transition_tmo or ALUA_FAILOVER_TIMEOUT) * HZ). A failed initial kzalloc returns SCSI_DH_DEV_TEMP_BUSY (the expiry may already have been set). It then calls submit_rtpg. If that returns non-zero: when pg->valid_states has no state other than TPGS_SUPPORT_OPTIMIZED it logs and returns SCSI_DH_OK; if the result is negative or the sense data is not valid it returns SCSI_DH_DEV_TEMP_BUSY for a negative result, SCSI_DH_RES_TEMP_UNAVAIL when host_byte(retval) == DID_NO_CONNECT, and SCSI_DH_IO otherwise (pg state and expiry unchanged); with valid sense: ILLEGAL_REQUEST while ALUA_RTPG_EXT_HDR_UNSUPP is not set sets that flag and resubmits; NOT_READY with asc 0x04 and ascq 0x0a skips the data parsing and marks the state transitioning below; UNIT_ATTENTION returns SCSI_DH_RETRY if pg->expiry is non-zero and jiffies is before it; any other case sets pg->expiry to 0 and returns SCSI_DH_IO. If submit_rtpg succeeds and the reported length exceeds the buffer it reallocates (a failed kmalloc sets pg->expiry to 0 and returns SCSI_DH_DEV_TEMP_BUSY) and resubmits. It then updates pg->transition_tmo from the extended header (or ALUA_FAILOVER_TIMEOUT), recomputing pg->expiry when it changed, and for each descriptor it finds the port group, and if its lock can be taken without waiting updates its state, preference and the sdevs' access_state (when it is pg itself or not running) and pg->valid_states for pg itself. Finally, under pg->lock, it sets pg->state to transitioning if the NOT_READY sense was seen, then returns by pg->state: transitioning with jiffies before expiry gives SCSI_DH_RETRY (pg->interval = ALUA_RTPG_RETRY_DELAY), transitioning past expiry gives SCSI_DH_IO (state set to standby, expiry 0, sdev access states updated), offline gives SCSI_DH_DEV_OFFLINED (expiry 0), any other state gives SCSI_DH_OK (expiry 0).
note: reviewer (round 15: RES_TEMP_UNAVAIL and the first IO return are for an invalid sense, not valid sense) right, scsi_dh_alua.c:588-598. The old prose also said pg was untouched on a failed kzalloc, but the expiry may be initialised first. Function at 535-775.

name: alua_rtpg_queue
prose: Precondition: pg may be NULL (WARN_ON_ONCE), sdev is a valid scsi_device, qdata (if non-NULL) is not already on a list, force requests queueing. Postcondition: if pg is NULL or scsi_device_get(sdev) fails it returns false with no other effect (qdata is not linked and stays owned by the caller). Otherwise, under pg->lock: if qdata is non-NULL it links qdata on pg->rtpg_list, sets ALUA_PG_RUN_STPG and forces queueing; if pg->rtpg_sdev is NULL and sdev's handler data belongs to pg it sets interval 0, ALUA_PG_RUN_RTPG, takes a pg kref, sets pg->rtpg_sdev = sdev and marks the work to be started; else if pg->rtpg_sdev is set, ALUA_PG_RUN_RTPG is not set and force is true it sets ALUA_PG_RUN_RTPG and, when ALUA_PG_RUNNING is not set, takes a pg kref and marks the work to be started. After unlocking, if the work is to be started it calls queue_delayed_work(kaluad_wq, &pg->rtpg_work, ALUA_RTPG_DELAY_MSECS); on success the sdev reference and pg kref pass to the work item, and on failure the pg kref is released and the sdev reference is dropped; if no work was started the sdev reference is dropped. It then returns true in all of those cases, including when queue_delayed_work failed or nothing was started; a qdata that was linked stays on pg->rtpg_list (even when no work was queued) for a later alua_rtpg_work run, so the caller must not free or reuse it.
note: reviewer (round 15: returns false when queue_delayed_work fails) wrong: scsi_dh_alua.c:1046-1056 ends with an unconditional 'return true'. Round 1 (qdata not linked when scsi_device_get fails) is reflected. Function at 1007-1057.

name: efc_cmd_node_detach
prose: Precondition: efc points to a driver context and rnode is NULL or a remote node. Postcondition: returns -EIO (with a log message) if rnode is NULL. If rnode->nport is non-NULL it returns -EIO when the node is not attached; otherwise it builds an UNREG_RPI command with sli_cmd_unreg_rpi and, if that call returns 0, issues it with efc->tt.issue_mbox_rqst using efc_cmd_node_free_cb and rnode as the callback and argument, returning 0 only when the issue call returns 0 (a failure to build or issue is logged and returns -EIO); the caller must not free rnode before the callback runs. If rnode->nport is NULL it returns -EIO too, because rc is initialised to -EIO and nothing sets it to 0 on that path.
note: listed name efc_cmd_node_free does not exist; the function is efc_cmd_node_detach (efc_cmds.c:754-782). The old prose said 'returns 0 if rnode has no nport', which is wrong: rc starts at -EIO (line 757).

name: efc_node_dispatch_frame
prose: Precondition: arg is a valid efc_node and seq a valid hardware sequence whose header buffer holds a frame header. Postcondition: returns nothing and does not free seq itself. If the source port id does not equal node->rnode.fc_id it issues WARN_ON and returns; if the frame lacks FC_FC_END_SEQ or FC_FC_SEQ_INIT it logs 'Drop frame' with the header words and returns. Otherwise it dispatches on r_ctl: ELS request/reply frames go to efc_node_recv_els_frame; BA_ABTS, BA_ACC, BA_RJT and BA_NOP only log 'Received ABTS'; unsolicited command/control frames of type FCP go to efc_node_recv_fcp_cmd when the low nibble of r_ctl is the command code and fcp_enabled is not set (otherwise an error is logged and the frame is dropped; solicited data is logged and dropped), CT frames go to efc_node_recv_ct_frame, and other types do nothing; any other r_ctl logs 'Unhandled frame rctl'.
note: 'unnamed frame dispatch handler' is efc_node_dispatch_frame (efc_domain.c:1023-1088). The source-id mismatch case uses WARN_ON, not a log message as the old prose said.

name: efc_vport_create_spec
prose: Precondition: efc is a valid driver context; the caller holds neither efc->vport_lock nor any lock it needs to keep. Postcondition: it takes efc->vport_lock with interrupts saved and, if an existing vport on efc->vport_list already has the same non-zero wwpn and non-zero wwnn, logs and returns NULL. Otherwise it allocates a zeroed efc_vport with GFP_ATOMIC; if that fails it returns NULL. On success it sets wwnn, wwpn, fc_id, enable_tgt, enable_ini, tgt_data and ini_data, adds the vport to the tail of efc->vport_list and returns it. The lock is released before every return.
note: 'unnamed vport allocation function (excerpt)' is efc_vport_create_spec (efc_nport.c:734-777); the slice starts at the allocation. The old prose omitted the duplicate-vport NULL return.

name: sli_page_count
prose: Precondition: none for safety; the result is the ceiling of bytes / page_size only when page_size is a power of two and the result fits in 32 bits. Postcondition: returns 0 when page_size is 0; otherwise returns (bytes + (page_size - 1)) >> __ffs(page_size), converted to u32, where __ffs gives the zero-based index of the lowest set bit of page_size; for a power-of-two page_size that is the ceiling of bytes divided by page_size, and for other page sizes it divides by the value of the lowest set bit instead. It reads and writes no state.
note: sli4.h:2001-2008. The earlier random-test counterexample (bytes=172, page_size=128, result 1) does not match the kernel code, where __ffs(128) is 7 and the result is (172+127)>>7 = 2; it matches a test harness that uses the one-based ffs, so the contract is left empty rather than re-submitted.

name: esas2r_write_fs
prose: Precondition: a is an adapter, buf points to count bytes of kernel memory (the declaration has no __user), off is the write offset. Postcondition: when off == 0 it reads the FS command header from buf (before checking count), computes the required buffer length from fs->command.length (only the header size for ESAS2R_FS_CMD_BEGINW) and returns -EINVAL if count is smaller than the header size; otherwise it reuses a->fs_api_buffer if it is large enough, or frees a too-small buffer and allocates a new coherent DMA buffer of the required size, or allocates one if there is none. For every call, if a->fs_api_buffer is NULL (including when that allocation failed) it returns -ENOMEM; if off is greater than the buffer size it returns 0; it reduces count to buffer_size - off when count + off exceeds the buffer, returns 0 if the resulting count is less than 1, and otherwise copies count bytes from buf into the buffer at off and returns count.
note: listed name fs_api_buffer_write_handler does not exist; the function is esas2r_write_fs (esas2r_ioctl.c:2020-2083). The old prose called buf a user buffer and said the -EINVAL check came first; the header is read before it.

name: hba_ioctl_callback
prose: Precondition: the buffered ioctl request (esas2r_buffered_ioctl) holds an atto_ioctl header; a, rq and sgc describe the adapter, request and scatter-gather context. Postcondition: it sets hi->status to ATTO_STS_SUCCESS and dispatches on hi->function: for adapter-info, adapter-address, device-address, device-info, adapter-control and similar functions it fills the reply and sets hi->status to a success or error code (ATTO_STS_UNSUPPORTED for tunnelled use of functions that are not tunnelled, ATTO_STS_INV_VERSION with the maximum version for a too-high version, ATTO_STS_FAILED, ATTO_STS_OUT_OF_RSRC, and ATTO_STS_INV_FUNC for an unknown function) and returns false; for MEM_RW, TRACE, SCSI_PASS_THRU, GET_DEV_ADDR, GET_DEV_INFO, PHY_CTRL and CONN_CTRL when a request was tunnelled (hba_ioctl_tunnel returned true), and for SCSI_PASS_THRU when it built the scatter-gather list and called esas2r_start_request, it returns true. Every other path returns false.
note: listed name hba_ioctl_dispatch does not exist; the function is hba_ioctl_callback (esas2r_ioctl.c:746-1196), declared int but returning true/false. Partly read: the head and tail, every case label and every return statement were read, and the MEM_RW, TRACE, SCSI_PASS_THRU, PHY_CTRL and GET_DEV_INFO cases partly; most case bodies (notably adapter-info, trace and adapter-control) were not read line by line.

name: esas2r_process_vda_ioctl
prose: Precondition: a, vi, rq and sgc are valid; sgc->cur_offset points into the ioctl data area. Postcondition: it sets vi->status to ATTO_STS_SUCCESS and vi->vda_status to RS_PENDING and returns false with vi->status set when: vi->function is out of range (ATTO_STS_INV_FUNC), vi->version exceeds the supported version for the function (ATTO_STS_INV_VERSION), or the adapter is in degraded mode (ATTO_STS_DEGRADED); these three returns happen before the request is touched. For every non-SCSI function it then clears the request (clear_vda_request), sets the function, interrupt_cb esas2r_complete_vda_ioctl and interrupt_cx vi, and handles the function: FLASH accepts sub_func FREAD, FWRITE or FINFO (other values return false with ATTO_STS_INV_FUNC), CLI, MGT (a non-zero data_length needs mgt_func DEV_HEALTH_REQ, DEV_METRICS, DEV_INFO2 or DEV_INFO2_BYADDR, otherwise ATTO_STS_INV_PARAM; a payload SGL build failure gives ATTO_STS_OUT_OF_RSRC), CFG (needs vi->data_length == 0 and cfg.data_length != 0, else ATTO_STS_INV_PARAM; VDA_CFG_INIT and any cfg_func other than VDA_CFG_GET_INIT give ATTO_STS_INV_FUNC), and GSV (sets vi->vda_status to RS_SUCCESS, rsp_len to the version count and copies the version table). VDA_FUNC_SCSI and any other value go to the default and return false with ATTO_STS_INV_FUNC. If the computed data length is non-zero it builds the scatter-gather list and returns false with ATTO_STS_OUT_OF_RSRC if that fails; otherwise it calls esas2r_start_request and returns true. After the first three checks a false return may leave the request partly initialised, so the caller must not submit it. No lock is taken.
note: reviewer (round 15: the shown code never returns true or calls esas2r_start_request) wrong: lines 264-266 do both; the packet slice ended at line 253, before them. The old text said the request may be cleared in every failure case, which is not so for the first three. Function at esas2r_vda.c:65-267.

name: esp_process_event
prose: Precondition: esp is a valid ESP host; esp->active_cmd points to a valid command entry for the events that dereference it. Postcondition: returns 1 when the event was handled and processing may continue, and 0 in these cases: esp_schedule_reset was called (unexpected phase, zero DMA length, DMA error, data done without a bus-service interrupt, a negative byte count, an unexpected message in the status or free-bus event, MSGIN with neither bus-service nor function-done, CMD_DONE without bus service, or an unknown event); ESP_EVENT_STATUS saw a bus-service interrupt, read the status byte and queued the MSGIN event; and ESP_EVENT_MSGIN found esp->event == ESP_EVENT_RESET after processing the message byte. The CHECK_PHASE status-phase case and the MSGIN bus-service case return 1 early (setting the quick-IRQ flag); other handled cases loop (goto again) or end with return 1. It may update esp->event, flags, message, DMA and FIFO state, complete the active command (via esp_cmd_is_done), start autosense, or start the next queued command.
note: listed name esp_do_dma does not exist; the function is esp_process_event (esp_scsi.c:1689-2026), read in full. The old prose missed the STATUS+BSERV return 0.

name: fcoe_ctlr_recv_adv
prose: Precondition: fip is a valid FCoE controller and skb a received FIP frame; it need not be a valid advertisement. Postcondition: returns nothing. If fcoe_ctlr_parse_adv rejects the frame it returns at once. Otherwise it holds fip->ctlr_mutex until it returns. If an FCF with the same switch_name, fabric_name, fc_map and fcf_mac exists it updates its fd_flags (copying flags only when it is not usable), adjusts ctlr_ka_time and re-arms fip->timer when it is the selected FCF with fd_flags clear, and copies fka_period and fcf_mac. If none exists: when fip->fcf_count is at the limit, kmalloc fails or fcoe_sysfs_fcf_add fails (the new FCF is then kfreed) it goes to the exit without doing any of the following; otherwise the new FCF has been added to fip->fcfs and fcf_count incremented by fcoe_sysfs_fcf_add. Only on the paths with an existing or newly added FCF it then sets fcf->time to jiffies, sends a solicited advertisement (fcoe_ctlr_solicit with the FCF) if its MTU is not yet validated, sends a multicast solicitation if the list was empty on entry and jiffies is past fip->sol_time + the solicit timeout, moves the FCF to the head of fip->fcfs when its MTU is valid, and, when its MTU is valid, no FCF is selected, no selection time is pending and the FCF is usable, sets fip->sel_time to jiffies + FCOE_CTLR_START_DELAY and arms fip->timer if none is pending or the new time is earlier.
note: reviewer (round 15: the limit, kmalloc and sysfs failures leave before the time/solicit/selection steps) right, fcoe_ctlr.c:1043-1059. Function at 1018-1127; fcoe_sysfs_fcf_add at 161-226 adds to the list.

name: fnic_init_module
prose: Precondition: module load; none of the fnic caches, workqueues, transport or PCI registration exist. Postcondition: it tries fnic_debugfs_init, fnic_trace_buf_init and fnic_fc_trace_init; a failure of each is non-fatal (an error message and the matching cleanup call, the return value is overwritten later). It then creates, in order, the fnic_sgl_dflt and fnic_sgl_max slab caches, fnic_io_req_cache, fdls_frame_cache, fdls_frame_elem_cache, the fnic_event_queue and fnic_fip_queue workqueues, the reset_fnic_work_queue only when pc_rscn_handling_feature_flag == PC_RSCN_HANDLING_FEATURE_ON, the FC transport with fc_attach_transport, and registers the PCI driver. It returns the result of pci_register_driver on success (0). Any earlier failure returns -ENOMEM (cache, workqueue or transport) or the negative pci_register_driver value, after unwinding the earlier steps in reverse order through the error labels and then calling fnic_trace_free, fnic_fc_trace_free and fnic_debugfs_terminate. The unwinding is not exact: when the reset workqueue creation fails, the label that is reached destroys fnic_event_queue but not fnic_fip_queue, which stays allocated. fnic_cleanup_module later releases everything except fdls_frame_elem_cache.
note: reviewer (round 15: on reset workqueue creation failure fnic_fip_queue is not destroyed, contradicting the exact-cleanup claim) right, fnic_main.c:1342-1346 jumping to 1374 skips 1370; round 2 (cleanup omits fdls_frame_elem_cache) also right, 1393-1413. Function at 1239-1391.

name: generic_NCR5380_init_one
prose: Precondition: pdev is the parent device, board is one of BOARD_NCR5380, BOARD_NCR53C400, BOARD_NCR53C400A, BOARD_DTC3181E or BOARD_HP_C2502, base is the I/O port (up to 0xffff) or the memory base, irq the requested IRQ. Postcondition: it returns 0 after allocating and adding a Scsi_Host, scanning it and setting pdev's drvdata to it, holding the reserved region, the mapping and a successfully requested IRQ until later release; a failed request_irq is not fatal (the host runs without an IRQ). It returns -EBUSY if the I/O region (or the memory region) cannot be reserved, or if a non-magic port-mapped board is given base 0; for a magic-sequence board (NCR53C400A, HP C2502, DTC3181E on a port-mapped base) it returns -EINVAL when the given base is not in the port list or no free port is found, and -ENODEV when the register readback at base + 9 is not 0x80 (releasing the region); it returns -ENOMEM if ioport_map/ioremap or scsi_host_alloc fails, -EINVAL for a memory-mapped DTC3181E, NCR53C400A or HP C2502 board (unknown register offsets), -ENODEV if the MODE register is not 0 after being cleared (vacant slot check), or the error from NCR5380_init or scsi_add_host. Failures after the region was reserved release what had been acquired in reverse (the IRQ and NCR5380_exit after scsi_add_host fails, then the host reference, the mapping and the region).
note: listed name generic_NCR5380_probe does not exist; the function is generic_NCR5380_init_one (g_NCR5380.c:223-465), read in full. The earlier prose put the failures under a platform-device probe and omitted the port-list and -EINVAL cases.

name: hisi_sas_queue_command
prose: Precondition: task is a sas_task whose dev is a domain device, gfp_flags says whether the caller may block. Postcondition: if the device's port is NULL it sets task_status to SAS_TASK_UNDELIVERED / SAS_PHY_DOWN, calls task->task_done unless the device is SATA or the task is an internal abort, and returns -ECOMM. For SSP, SMP, SATA and STP tasks: if HISI_SAS_REJECT_CMD_BIT is set it returns -EINVAL when gfp_flags does not allow blocking, otherwise takes and releases hisi_hba->sem and continues; it returns -ECOMM when the device is gone or the port is not attached; it chooses the delivery queue from the request's block tag when the task has a request, queue 0 when iopoll queues exist, else the current CPU's default queue map. For an internal abort it returns TMF_RESP_FUNC_FAILED when the hardware has no prep_abort, -EIO when the hardware-fault bit is set, -EINVAL when the reject bit is set, and uses the queue given by abort_task.qid; an unknown task protocol returns -EINVAL. It then maps the DMA buffers and, for non-ATA protocols, the DIF buffers, and allocates a slot index; a failure of any of these returns the negative error after undoing the mappings it had made (no slot is left allocated) and logging. On success it fills the slot and calls hisi_sas_task_deliver and returns 0.
note: listed name hisi_sas_task_prep does not exist in this tree; the slice 508-758 lies in hisi_sas_queue_command (hisi_sas_main.c:493-647), which contains exactly the logic the old prose described.

name: phy_up_v2_hw
prose: Precondition: phy_no indexes a valid phy of hisi_hba and a phy-up interrupt is pending so its registers are readable. Postcondition: returns an int (IRQ_HANDLED or IRQ_NONE). It writes 1 to PHYCTRL_PHY_ENA_MSK; for a SATA phy it skips to the common exit. Otherwise it deletes phy->timer, reads the port id and link rate (from PORT_STATE for phy 8, else from PHY_PORT_NUM_MA and PHY_CONN_RATE); if the port id is 0xf it logs an error and sets the result to IRQ_NONE, skipping the phy-up processing. Otherwise it reads six dwords from RX_IDAF_DWORD0.., byte-swaps each into sas_phy->frame_rcvd (the local frame_rcvd pointer aliases sas_phy->frame_rcvd), sets sas_phy->linkrate and oob_mode, copies the attached SAS address from the identify frame, sets phy->port_id, marks the phy attached with SAS port type, copies the identify device type, sets frame_rcvd_size to the identify frame size, sets target_port_protocols to SSP for an end device or to SMP for another used device type (arming the link-timer quirk when the hba timer is not pending), and notifies HISI_PHYE_PHY_UP. In every case, including SATA phys and the invalid port id, at the exit it completes phy->reset_completion if non-NULL, writes CHL_INT0_SL_PHY_ENABLE_MSK to CHL_INT0 and writes 0 to PHYCTRL_PHY_ENA_MSK, and returns the result (IRQ_HANDLED unless the port id was invalid).
note: reviewer (round 15: it only fills a local frame_rcvd and never copies it) wrong: frame_rcvd is declared as (u32 *)sas_phy->frame_rcvd (hisi_sas_v2_hw.c:2653), so the stores at 2686 go straight into sas_phy->frame_rcvd; round 2's complaint about the identify frame is consistent with that. Function at 2646-2717.

name: ibmvfc_npiv_login_done
prose: Precondition: evt is a completed NPIV login event; the vhost login response buffer holds the firmware's reply. Postcondition: returns nothing and calls ibmvfc_free_event(evt) on every path. For MAD status IBMVFC_MAD_FAILED it either calls ibmvfc_retry_host_init (when ibmvfc_retry_cmd accepts the response status and error) or moves the host to a dead link, logs the failure and returns. For IBMVFC_MAD_CRQ_ERROR it calls ibmvfc_retry_host_init and returns; for IBMVFC_MAD_DRIVER_FAILED it only frees the event and returns (no retry); for any unrecognised status it logs and moves the host to a dead link. For IBMVFC_MAD_SUCCESS it clears client_migrated; if the response lacks IBMVFC_NATIVE_FC, or max_cmds is at most IBMVFC_NUM_INTERNAL_REQ, it moves the host to a dead link and wakes work_wait_q without setting logged_in. Otherwise it sets logged_in to 1, copies the fabric, node and port names, port id, port type NPIV, supported classes and maxframe size into the fc_host attributes, sets can_queue to max_cmds - IBMVFC_NUM_INTERNAL_REQ and max_sectors, and then, if the channels capability is supported and do_enquiry is set, calls ibmvfc_channel_enquiry, else it clears do_enquiry, sets the host action to IBMVFC_HOST_ACTION_QUERY and wakes work_wait_q.
note: reviewer (round 15: DRIVER_FAILED does not schedule a retry, only CRQ_ERROR does) right, ibmvfc.c:5208-5213. The effect of ibmvfc_channel_enquiry on failure was not read. Function at 5186-5270.

name: ibmvscsis_disconnect
prose: Precondition: work is the proc_work member of an initialised scsi_info; process context; the caller does not hold vscsi->intr_lock. Postcondition: returns nothing; it takes intr_lock with spin_lock_bh and releases it before returning, saves vscsi->new_state, sets new_state to 0, sets DISCONNECT_SCHEDULED and clears SCHEDULE_DISCONNECT, and then by vscsi->state: NO_QUEUE and UNCONFIGURING stay unchanged; ERR_DISCONNECT, ERR_DISCONNECTED and UNDEFINED move to UNCONFIGURING only when the saved new_state is UNCONFIGURING; ERR_DISCONNECT_RECONNECT moves to UNCONFIGURING or ERR_DISCONNECT when the saved new_state is one of those and otherwise stays; WAIT_ENABLED with new_state UNCONFIGURING sets the state, sets RESPONSE_Q_DOWN, clears SCHEDULE_DISCONNECT and DISCONNECT_SCHEDULED and, if CFG_SLEEPING was set, clears it and completes vscsi->unconfig, with ERR_DISCONNECT, ERR_DISCONNECT_RECONNECT or WAIT_IDLE as new_state it only logs dev_err and leaves the state, and any other new_state does nothing; WAIT_IDLE with UNCONFIGURING sets RESPONSE_Q_DOWN, the state, clears the two flags and calls ibmvscsis_free_command_q with the lock held, and with ERR_DISCONNECT or ERR_DISCONNECT_RECONNECT sets the state; WAIT_CONNECTION, CONNECTED and SRP_PROCESSING set the state to new_state and mark a wait for idle: if either the active or schedule queue is non-empty it sets WAIT_FOR_IDLE, drops the lock, waits for vscsi->wait_idle (no timeout) and retakes the lock, and in both cases calls ibmvscsis_adapter_idle; other state and new_state combinations leave the state unchanged.
note: reviewer (round 15: WAIT_ENABLED logs dev_err only for ERR_DISCONNECT, ERR_DISCONNECT_RECONNECT and WAIT_IDLE, not for any other new_state) right, ibmvscsi_tgt.c:485-490. Function at 409-557; slice cut the head.

name: ips_module_init
prose: Precondition: none; called at module load. Postcondition: on platforms other than x86, ia64 and x86_64 it first logs and taints the kernel. It calls pci_register_driver(&ips_pci_driver) and returns -ENODEV (-19) without registering the reboot notifier if that fails. Otherwise it sets ips_driver_template.module, calls ips_order_controllers and ips_detect; if ips_detect returns 0 it unregisters the PCI driver and returns -ENODEV. Otherwise it registers the reboot notifier with register_reboot_notifier and returns 0.
note: ips.c:6714-6731. Contract dropped because the function sets globals and registers notifiers; reviewer (round 15: contract weaker than prose) was only about that omission.

name: sci_io_request_frame_handler
prose: Precondition: ireq is an isci_request in some state and frame_index names an unsolicited frame owned by the controller. Postcondition: it dispatches on the request state machine state. SCI_REQ_STARTED: an SSP response frame is copied into ireq->ssp.rsp and the scu/sci status set (check-response and a controller-specific error status when the data presence is response or sense data, good otherwise); a non-response frame is only logged; the frame is released and SCI_SUCCESS returned. SCI_REQ_TASK_WAIT_TC_RESP: copies the response, moves to SCI_REQ_COMPLETED, releases the frame and returns SCI_SUCCESS. SCI_REQ_SMP_WAIT_RESP: copies the SMP response into the task's smp_resp buffer (moving to SCI_REQ_SMP_WAIT_TC_COMP) or on a non-response frame sets the frame-type-error statuses and moves to SCI_REQ_COMPLETED, then releases the frame and returns SCI_SUCCESS. SCI_REQ_STP_UDMA_WAIT_TC_COMP returns whatever sci_stp_request_udma_general_frame_handler returns; SCI_REQ_STP_UDMA_WAIT_D2H calls it and, if it returns SCI_SUCCESS, sets a check-response status and moves to SCI_REQ_COMPLETED, otherwise returns its status. SCI_REQ_STP_NON_DATA_WAIT_D2H, SCI_REQ_STP_PIO_WAIT_FRAME and SCI_REQ_STP_PIO_DATA_IN first get the frame header and return the non-success status (without releasing the frame) if that fails; then a D2H register FIS completes the request with a response-valid status (or a protocol violation status in the non-data state for other FIS types), a PIO setup FIS records the transfer length and status and moves to the PIO data-in state or transmits data for data-out (a transmit failure returns that status), PIO data-in copies the data (or saves the frame index in ireq->saved_rx_frame_index when no buffer is available) and moves to completed or back to PIO wait frame when the transfer finishes, and the frame is released except in the deferred data-in case. SCI_REQ_ATAPI_WAIT_PIO_SETUP releases the frame, starts the next ATAPI step and returns SCI_SUCCESS; SCI_REQ_ATAPI_WAIT_D2H returns atapi_d2h_reg_frame_handler's result; SCI_REQ_ABORTING releases the frame and returns SCI_SUCCESS; any other state logs, releases the frame and returns SCI_FAILURE_INVALID_STATE.
note: 'sci_stp_request_frame_handler' is sci_io_request_frame_handler (request.c:1697-2092). The old prose did not describe the SSP, ATAPI, aborting and default-state returns and said the frame is released only where the header was obtained, which does not hold for the default and ABORTING states. The UDMA general and ATAPI D2H helpers were not read.

name: sas_rediscover_dev
prose: Precondition: dev is an expander domain device whose ex_phy[phy_id] is valid; last says whether phy_id is the last phy of its wide port; sibling is used only in the debug message. Postcondition: it returns -ENOMEM at once if allocating the SMP discover response buffer fails; otherwise it frees the buffer before every later return. It calls sas_get_phy_discover and: for SMP_RESP_NO_PHY or SMP_RESP_PHY_VACANT it marks the phy not-present or vacant, unregisters the devices on that phy address and returns that positive code; for any result other than SMP_RESP_FUNC_ACC and -ECOMM it returns the result unchanged. If the SAS address read from the response (res == 0) is 0, or res is -ECOMM, it marks the phy empty, unregisters the devices, updates the phy info when res is 0 and returns res (0 or -ECOMM). If the address and device type are unchanged (flutter) it re-runs sas_ex_phy_discover and returns 0. Otherwise it unregisters the old devices and returns the result of sas_discover_new, whether that is 0 or an error.
note: reviewer (round 15: omits that a changed device returns sas_discover_new's result, including success 0) right, sas_expander.c:2038-2041. Function at 1965-2042.

name: sas_smp_host_handler
prose: Precondition: job is a bsg job whose request and reply payload scatter lists are valid, shost belongs to a libsas host. Postcondition: returns nothing; it ends every path with bsg_job_done(job, error, reslen). If either payload length is below 8 it completes with -EINVAL and reslen 0 without allocating. It allocates a zeroed request buffer (-ENOMEM on failure) and copies the request in, then a zeroed response buffer of at least 128 bytes (-ENOMEM on failure, freeing the request buffer); if req_data[0] is not SMP_REQUEST, or SMP_DISCOVER or SMP_REPORT_PHY_SATA has a request shorter than 16 bytes, or SMP_PHY_CONTROL has a request shorter than 44 bytes, it completes with -EINVAL, reslen 0 and nothing copied to the reply. Otherwise the default response is 'function unknown' and the switch fills it for the supported functions (report general, manufacturer info, discover, report phy SATA, write GPIO register, phy control), setting reslen to 32, 64, 56, 60, 8 and 8 respectively; a write-GPIO request shorter than its computed size sets SMP_RESP_INV_FRM_LEN and leaves reslen 0; unsupported functions keep the default response and reslen 0. The response buffer is copied into the reply payload, error is 0, both buffers are freed, and the job is completed with error 0 and reslen.
note: listed name sas_host_smp_handler does not exist; the function is sas_smp_host_handler (sas_host_smp.c:225-354). The old prose said both buffers are freed 'in every path'; on the early -EINVAL and -ENOMEM paths one or both were never allocated.

name: sas_class_init
prose: Precondition: called once at module load (__init). Postcondition: it creates sas_task_cache and then sas_event_cache with KMEM_CACHE; it returns 0 if both succeed, -ENOMEM if the first fails (nothing to undo), and -ENOMEM after destroying sas_task_cache if the second fails.
note: sas_init.c:681-696. Contract dropped because the function assigns globals.

name: #define lpfc_param_init(attr, default, minval, maxval)
prose: Macro-generated function: lpfc_param_init(attr, default, minval, maxval) expands to a static function lpfc_<attr>_init(struct lpfc_hba *phba, uint val). If lpfc_rangecheck(val, minval, maxval) accepts val it stores val in phba->cfg_<attr> and returns 0; otherwise it logs an error (message 0449) saying the allowed range, stores the macro's default value in phba->cfg_<attr> and returns -EINVAL.
note: macro at lpfc_attr.c:2860-2873. The old contract used 'default' as a logic variable. Left empty because the function writes through phba.

name: #define lpfc_vport_param_init(attr, default, minval, maxval)
prose: Macro-generated function: lpfc_vport_param_init(attr, default, minval, maxval) expands to a static function lpfc_<attr>_init(struct lpfc_vport *vport, uint val). If lpfc_rangecheck(val, minval, maxval) accepts val it stores val in vport->cfg_<attr> and returns 0; otherwise it logs an error (message 0423) with the allowed range, stores the default in vport->cfg_<attr> and returns -EINVAL.
note: macro at lpfc_attr.c:3019-3032.

name: lpfc_bsg_diag_loopback_run
prose: Precondition: job is a bsg diagnostic loopback request. Postcondition: it clears reply_payload_rcv_len and returns a negative errno through the common exit (setting bsg_reply->result to the return value and job->dd_data to NULL; the job is completed with bsg_job_done only when the result is 0): -EINVAL if the request is shorter than the minimum or the request and reply payload lengths differ, -EACCES if the HBA is in error, management I/O is blocked, SLI is not active, the link is down or not in loopback mode, -ERANGE if the payload size is 0 or over 80 * 4096 bytes, -ENOMEM if the data buffer allocation fails, or the error of lpfcdiag_loop_self_reg; none of those releases anything beyond the data buffer. After registering the loopback RPI, on SLI3 it gets the xri and posts receive buffers (failure unregisters the RPI and returns that error). It then creates an event, takes IOCBs and a BDE list; allocation failure returns -ENOMEM through the cleanup path, sending the loopback frame and a non-success wait result or ULP status returns -EIO, a missing unsolicited event returns -EINTR (when time_left is non-zero) or -ETIMEDOUT, and a received length different from the expected one or no data returns -EIO. On success it copies the received data into the reply payload, sets reply_payload_rcv_len to size and returns 0. The cleanup path unregisters the loopback RPI, drops both event references, releases the command IOCB (except after IOCB_TIMEDOUT), the response IOCB and the BDE buffers, and frees the data buffer.
note: listed name lpfc_bsg_diag_loopback_test does not exist; the function is lpfc_bsg_diag_loopback_run (lpfc_bsg.c:3035-3328), read in full. The old prose omitted -EINVAL, -EACCES and -ERANGE and said the RPI was unregistered on every error.

name: lpfc_idiag_pcicfg_read
prose: Precondition: file->private_data is a lpfc_debug whose i_private is a lpfc_hba; *ppos is the file position. Postcondition: it returns 0 if phba->pcidev is NULL. Otherwise it sets debug->op to LPFC_IDIAG_OP_RD, allocates debug->buffer (LPFC_PCI_CFG_SIZE) if needed and returns 0 if that fails, returns 0 if *ppos is non-zero or the pending idiag command opcode is not LPFC_IDIAG_CMD_PCICFG_RD. For a count of 1, 2 or 4 bytes it reads that PCI config register at the given offset and formats 'offset: value'; for an illegal count it formats nothing (len 0); for LPFC_PCI_CFG_BROWSE it formats LPFC_PCI_CFG_RD_SIZE bytes of config space starting at idiag.offset.last_rd in rows of 8 dwords (stopping early at the end of config space) and then advances idiag.offset.last_rd by LPFC_PCI_CFG_RD_SIZE, wrapping to 0 at the end, or resets it to 0 if the read stopped early. In the single-register, illegal-count and browse cases it returns the result of simple_read_from_buffer: the bytes copied, 0 at EOF (always for an empty buffer), or a negative error.
note: reviewer (round 15: the illegal-count default returns 0 without formatting) right, lpfc_debugfs.c:3371-3376 (it calls simple_read_from_buffer with len 0, which returns 0). Function at 3317-3417.
